National Geographic Magazine. Founded in 1888 by the National Geographic Society, it is an illustrated journal of exploration, natural science, and world culture. It began as a scholarly journal and evolved into a mass-market magazine. Circulation grew to nearly twelve million in the late twentieth century and was translated into multiple languages and distributed worldwide. National Geographic became famous for its color photography of nature and remote places, elevating magazine photography to both an art form and a scientific documentation tool. The magazine published photographs by renowned photographers including Robert Capa, Steve Winter, and Joel Sartore. National Geographic is known for expedition documentation, funding and chronicling explorations of Mount Everest, the Galápagos, and polar regions. The editorial mission combined scientific education, cultural documentation, and adventurous storytelling about the natural world and human societies. The distinctive yellow-bordered cover became iconic and instantly recognizable worldwide. Through its work, National Geographic funded and documented major scientific expeditions, pioneered color photography in magazines, and brought natural science to mass audiences while documenting and shaping Western views of non-Western peoples.
